title: Vanda Inacio
text:
About me
I am a Reader (equivalent to an Associate Professor outside the UK) in the School of Mathematics at the University of Edinburgh, where I am currently Director of Teaching.
My time is split between research, teaching, and administration — and I actually enjoy all three. My research may not — or rather, will not — change the world, but I firmly believe that we can change lives through education that is free or, at the very least, accessible.

title: Vanda Inacio
text:
Research
I work in biostatistics, mainly on the statistical evaluation of biomarkers and diagnostic tests: how well they distinguish between disease stages, and how factors such as age and gender change that accuracy. I use both Bayesian and frequentist (nonparametric) methods, with a preference for the former.
I developed some of the first methods for inference about several summary measures of diagnostic accuracy — the partial area under the ROC curve, the Youden index and the covariate-adjusted ROC curve — that make no assumptions about the distribution of test outcomes in each population, or about how covariates relate to those outcomes. I also introduced the first measure of diagnostic accuracy that accounts for a functional (curve-valued) covariate (Biostatistics, 2012).
More recently, with colleagues, I proposed the underlap coefficient, a measure of how well a biomarker distinguishes between more than two disease stages (Biometrics, 2026).
Many of these methods are freely available in the R package ROCnReg. More details are on the Publications and Software pages.

title: Software
text:
ROC curve inference with and without covariates · R package · CRAN · Paper · Talk (YouTube, 50 min) · 
ROCnReg estimates ROC curves and related summaries of discriminatory accuracy, using both frequentist and Bayesian methods. When it was released, it was the only R package implementing Bayesian procedures for ROC curves.

Pooled, covariate-specific and covariate-adjusted ROC curves
Parametric, semiparametric and nonparametric estimators, within both the Bayesian and frequentist paradigms
Summary measures such as the (partial) area under the curve and the Youden index
ROC-based optimal thresholds under several criteria (e.g., the Youden index)
For the Bayesian methods: model checking via posterior predictive checks and model choice via information criteria
Numerical and graphical output for all methods

install.packages("ROCnReg")
How to cite: Rodriguez-Alvarez, M.X. and Inacio, V. (2021). ROCnReg: An R package for receiver operating characteristic curve inference with and without covariates. The R Journal, 13, 525–555. doi:10.32614/RJ-2021-066

title: Software
text:
DDPstar
Bayesian nonparametric density regression · R package · CRAN · Paper · Talk (YouTube) · 
DDPstar fits a flexible and computationally tractable model for density regression, based on a single-weights dependent Dirichlet process mixture of normal distributions for a univariate continuous response.

Additive structure for the mean of each mixture component
Smooth nonlinear effects of continuous covariates via penalised B-splines and their bivariate tensor-product extension
Also handles parametric effects of categorical covariates, linear effects, interactions, varying-coefficient terms and random effects

install.packages("DDPstar")
How to cite: Rodriguez-Alvarez, M.X., Inacio, V. and Klein, N. (2025). Density regression via Dirichlet process mixtures of normal structured additive regression models. Statistics and Computing, 35, 47. doi:10.1007/s11222-025-10567-0
Note: a faster C++ implementation of the DDPstar sampler, the R package ddpfast, was introduced in a contributed discussion (p. 58) of MacEachern’s Dependent Dirichlet Processes in Bayesian Analysis.
